metric_name: Overall PA Denial Rate (MA - Full or Partial)
notes: 4.1M of 52.8M determinations denied in full or part in 2024. Use as baseline denial rate. Note: 2023 was 6.4% (S4); use 7.7% as current baseline.
use_in_project: Yes - baseline denial rate in synthetic data

metric_name: Overall PA Denial Rate (MA 2023)
notes: 3.2M of 49.8M determinations denied in 2023. Use for year-over-year trend simulation.

metric_name: Share of Denied PAs That Are Appealed
notes: Only 11.5% of denied PAs are appealed (11.7% in 2023). Very low appeal uptake despite high overturn rates. Critical for appeal funnel simulation.
use_in_project: Yes - appeal rate in synthetic data

metric_name: Appeal Overturn Rate (Partial or Full)
notes: 80.7% of appealed denials partially or fully overturned in 2024. Signals significant upstream decision error rate. Use as appeal overturn rate.
use_in_project: Yes - appeal outcome in synthetic data

metric_name: Share of Denied PAs That Met Coverage Rules (Inappropriate Denials)
notes: OIG stratified random sample found 13% of MA PA denials met Medicare coverage rules and should have been approved. Use to calibrate inappropriate denial rate in synthetic data. Note: based on 2019 study period; may have improved since.
use_in_project: Yes - denial reason / quality flag in synthetic data

metric_name: Standard PA Decision Turnaround Time (Current Industry)
notes: Industry current range: 3-7 calendar days for standard (non-urgent) requests. CMS-0057-F mandates ≤7 days beginning 2026. Use midpoint of 5 days as mean for lognormal turnaround distribution.
use_in_project: Yes - turnaround time distribution

metric_name: Urgent PA Decision Turnaround Time (Current Industry)
notes: Industry range: 24-72 hours (1-3 days) for urgent/expedited requests. CMS-0057-F mandates ≤72 hours beginning 2026. Use 1.5 days as mean for urgent distribution.
use_in_project: Yes - turnaround time distribution

metric_name: Post-Denial Rework / End-to-End Time
notes: Denied PAs requiring resubmission take 10-21+ days end-to-end. Use 15 days as mean for denied-and-reworked path in synthetic data.
use_in_project: Yes - rework time in synthetic data

metric_name: SLA Compliance Rate - Standard Requests (Current Payer Ops)
notes: No single public source gives exact SLA compliance rates. Assumption: ~82% of standard requests decided within 7-day CMS mandate. Based on industry gap analysis context. Label clearly as assumption in reporting.

metric_name: SLA Compliance Rate - Urgent Requests (Current Payer Ops)

use_in_project: Yes - SLA breach flag in synthetic data

metric_name: PA Volume per MA Plan per Year (Typical Mid-Size Plan)

metric_name: Documentation Incomplete Rate on First Submission
source_name: OIG S5 + AMA S8 + payer workflow assumption
notes: OIG found documentation issues were a primary cause of inappropriate denials (S5). AMA reports 94% of physicians face PA delays often tied to documentation back-and-forth (S8). 22% incomplete-on-first-submission is a documented payer workflow assumption — not a directly measured public figure. Label accordingly.
use_in_project: Yes - documentation flag in synthetic data; labeled assumption

metric_name: Pend Rate (Requests Held for Additional Information)
notes: No single public source gives pend rates directly. Pend (hold for more info) is standard PA workflow step. 12% is a conservative payer workflow assumption consistent with incomplete documentation rate. Label clearly as assumption.
use_in_project: Yes - decision_outcome = pended in synthetic data; clearly labeled assumption

metric_name: Denial Reason - Documentation Incomplete
notes: OIG (S5) identified documentation as primary inappropriate denial driver. Industry estimates documentation issues cause 25-30% of denials. Use 28% as documentation-related denial share.
use_in_project: Yes - denial_reason_category distribution

metric_name: Denial Reason - Medical Necessity Not Met

use_in_project: Yes - denial_reason_category distribution

metric_name: Denial Reason - Clinical Criteria Not Met (MAO-Specific)

metric_name: Denial Reason - Not a Covered Benefit

metric_name: Denial Reason - Duplicate or Administrative Error

metric_name: Electronic Submission Rate (Provider to Payer)
notes: CMS-0057-F PA API requirement for 2027 is driving electronic submission growth. Aetna processes 83% in real time (S7) but this implies significant electronic volume. 55% electronic, 25% fax, 20% portal/phone is a reasonable current baseline. Label as assumption.
use_in_project: Yes - submission_channel field in synthetic data

metric_name: Fax Submission Rate

metric_name: Portal/Phone Submission Rate
notes: Portal and phone submissions make up the remainder. 20% is consistent with industry context.

metric_name: Urgent Request Share of Total PA Volume

metric_name: First-Pass Approval Rate (Approved on Initial Submission)
